root.name: King's Gambit Accepted: McDonnell Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. Nc3

overview: After 4.Bc4 g4 White leaves the knight on f3 en prise with 5.Nc3, in the style of the Muzio, offering a piece for an attack on f7 and the open f-file. If Black plays 5...gxf3 6.Qxf3 White has a piece less for a pawn and gets fast development against a king that has lost its g-pawn. Black has safer alternatives, such as holding the extra pawn with ...Bg7 or ...Bh6 ideas, and the objective verdict is that the attack is not enough. I am unsure of the exact sub-line theory.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on f3 with the queen and aim at f7 with Bc4, Qxf7 and castling
Open the f-file with O-O and use the lead in development against the king

black_ideas.idea: Take the piece and return material at the right moment, e.g. ...Bg7 and ...d6
Keep the extra f4 pawn and develop with ...Nc6 and ...d6

typical_structures.structure: Open position, Black pawn on f4 and broken kingside pawns, White pieces aimed at f7

character.notes: Piece sacrifice for the attack and open f-file; forcing and risky for both sides.

gambit.notes: White has already lost the f-pawn and now leaves the f3 knight en prise to ...gxf3; Black can keep the material.

soundness.notes: Muzio-type sacrifices are considered unsound against accurate defence; the bishop on c4 and queen on f3 give practical chances only.

structure.notes: Open lines and the f-file, no central pawn tension.

approach.notes: Played by gambit specialists, seldom by strong players today.

level.notes: Sharp theory-led attack; a risky line rather than a first repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Salvio Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. Ne5
sublines_that_differ.how: The main line, with a sound knight outpost; this root is the piece-sacrifice alternative.

character.reason: A piece sacrifice for a direct attack on f7 leaves both kings exposed.

gambit.reason: White gives a pawn already and a piece after 5...gxf3, and Black may keep it.

soundness.reason: Muzio-style piece sacrifices are thought insufficient against correct defence.

structure.reason: The f-file and diagonals open at once and the game turns on piece activity.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose this sideline of the King's Gambit.

level.reason: A theory-driven attack that is not a good first repertoire pick but not deep enough to be Advanced.

plans.reason: White's compensation is the attack on f7 and faster development.
